response.final_text:
**Proposed disposition:** CLOSE_FP. Confidence is 0.85. A human analyst still has to decide.

**What drove it:**
1. The 17,528 BUY order (O-00023657) was an ICEBERG sitting at the touch (distance 0.0 ticks). It was already executing. 2,990 filled before any opposite-side trade, which is 17.1% of the quantity submitted and more than the 438 opposite fill. That means the order was working, so the first core feature (an order not meant to execute) is absent.
2. The 438 SELL was a separate LIMIT order under a different parent (C-T-X1028-06-B, against C-T-X1028-06-A for the BUY). This is an agency desk, so the SELL is a different client's order, not a round trip. Price move was 0.0 ticks and reversion was 0.0 ticks, so there was no benefit from the opposite-side trade.
3. There was one cycle in the session, no market events, and no prior alerts for this trader in 90 days. Size alone (7.2× average depth) does not count as a feature when the order is hidden and there is no benefit.

**What would change my mind:** evidence that the SELL under parent B belonged to the same beneficial owner as the BUY iceberg. Other things that would also change it are a favourable price move, or the same cycle repeating in other sessions.
